assumptions: The complete potential, curvature, initialization law and step conditions are stated above. No operator, probability, stationarity, mean-zero preservation or coercivity certificate is supplied by the caller.
L² consists of AE classes; finite dimension of E does not make L² finite dimensional. The whole closed mean-zero subspace is used.
Zero-dimensional E is explicitly included as an extension of the source Euclidean convention; αη=1 is retained.
units.statement: E is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert Borel space with canonical volume; rank zero is an explicit extension of the source Euclidean convention. V:E→ℝ is C²; 0<α≤β; α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v; η>0 and βη≤1. μ=volume.tilted(−V), J=Law(X,X+√ηZ) for independent X∼μ and Z∼N(0,I), and ν=J.snd. Finite dimensionality of E does not imply finite dimensionality of L²(ν). Let Λ be the law of (Y,2X−Y) under J, F(x,y)=(x,2x−y), and P the L²(J) conditional-expectation orthogonal projection onto the second-coordinate sigma algebra. The laws μ,J,ν are probabilities. There exist a Markov kernel S with, for every y, S(y)=volume.tilted(x↦−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)), Λ disintegrated by S and both marginals equal to ν; an involutive selfadjoint linear isometry U with Ug=g∘F J-a.e.; an isometric pullback M with Mu=u∘snd J-a.e.; and a selfadjoint T on L²(ν) such that for every u, PMu=Mu, MTu=PUPMu, ‖Tu‖≤‖u‖, Tu(y)=∫u(x)S(y,dx) ν-a.e. and ∫Tu dν=∫u dν. There is a constant class q=1 ν-a.e. with Tq=q and ⟨q,u⟩=∫u dν for all u. Its exact closed orthogonal kernel H₀ is all of L²₀(ν). The full defect D=I−T² is positive, Dq=0 and ⟨Du,u⟩=‖u‖²−‖Tu‖² for all u. The actual restriction T₀:H₀→H₀ agrees with T on every u∈H₀, is selfadjoint and contractive. D₀=I_H₀−T₀² is positive, agrees with D as an ambient L² class on H₀, and satisfies ⟨D₀u,u⟩=‖u‖²−‖T₀u‖² for all u∈H₀.

steps.title: Recover the actual kernel and Hilbert operators
steps.text: Reuse the compiled actual Gaussian augmentation, reflected conditional kernel S, isometric reflection U, second-coordinate pullback M, and operator T. The kernel has the literal normalized density exp(−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)); its stationary law and probability normalization are conclusions, not supplied premises.

steps.title: Transport selfadjointness
steps.text: The actual conditional expectation P is an orthogonal projection and U is selfadjoint. Move P across the inner product and use PM=M; the isometry M transfers the resulting symmetry to T.

steps.title: Prove mean preservation with the actual joint law
steps.text: The reflected joint law Λ disintegrates as ν⊗S and has second marginal ν. Each L² function is integrable because ν is a probability. The actual AE formula for T and Fubini therefore give mean preservation.

steps.title: Identify the constant and the entire centered space
steps.text: Take the canonical L² constant q=1. Its inner product is the mean. Selfadjointness and mean preservation imply Tq=q. The kernel of the continuous functional inner(q,·) is exactly all mean-zero classes, is closed, and is preserved by T.

steps.title: Restrict the actual operator
steps.text: Restrict T to the closed invariant subspace H₀. Its action as an ambient L² class is exactly T; symmetry and the norm bound transfer to this same restriction T₀.

steps.title: Compute both squared defects
steps.text: For either selfadjoint contraction, move one copy of T across the inner product. The result is nonnegative, so D=I−T² and D₀=I−T₀² are positive. Dq=0, and the centered defect is the actual restriction of D.
